media.alt: The site scrolling: a numbered rail down the left, three figures in draped white on black
media.caption: The numbering rail: a flick charges a flywheel, and the numbers coast to a stop.
Inside a project: long air between photographs, credits in a belt along the foot.
The clicked cover flies into place and leads the gallery.
Editions: eight works on one field, inquiry only.
About: the statement set in columns, the page locked to the viewport.
On a phone, one photograph at a time beside a lane of numbers you drag like a strip.

columns.text: Emilio Tamez wanted a site where nothing performs except the photographs, so it behaves like an object you turn in your hands. Twenty-four works hang on a single column of numbers with no beginning and no end. "If I just roll my finger fast, it keeps running until it loses traction," she said, and the column became a flywheel. Each time it comes back around, a work shows a different face, changed while no one is looking.

Nothing here feels like loading a page. Click a photograph and it flies into its gallery; close the project and the last picture you looked at flies home and stays on as the cover. Fashion waits behind one switch, the same instrument tuned dark. She runs the site herself, and published thirty times on her first day.
